Subject: Proposed edge fanout pattern for Acme private VPC - first pass

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Attached is a first-pass diagram showing the edge fanout topology we discussed for Acme’s private deployment: single control-plane fronting multiple localized data-plane clusters (on-prem racks + cloud edge hosts). The goal is to minimize cross-site egress while keeping the control plane logically central for policy, metrics, and rollouts.

Key asks from our side:
- Can Redwood operate with the control-plane in the customer VPC (no internet egress) and a thin outbound relay for telemetry?
- How would the KV cache and prefix caching work across the fanout (consistency/TTL implications)?
- Any constraints you foresee for mTLS trust domains across on-prem clusters?

Attachments: edge-fanout_v1.drawio.png (diagram), rough latency table in the diagram notes.

We’re targeting a review call next week — propose Tue 19th 10:00 PT. If that works for you I’ll send an invite and a readout template.

Hi Alicia — thanks for the diagram, this is a great starting point. I shared this with the infra/ops and runtime teams and pulled a few items for the review so we can be concrete on tradeoffs. Quick answers up front:

- Control-plane-in-VPC: yes, we support a private control plane in-customer VPC. The control plane needs to talk to the Dedicated/Private agents over a mutually authenticated channel; that channel can be strictly VPC-internal if the deployment model is fully on-prem with a peered management network.
- Telemetry relay: we can use an outbound-only telemetry relay that batches metrics and audited logs to a collector in the customer VPC or into a partner collector. We will need an approved egress ACL (see request below) and a small ephemeral TLS tunnel for push metrics when on-prem clusters are isolated.
- KV cache: local KV caches live on the data-plane nodes; we support prefix caching with configurable TTL per model version. Cross-site cache warming is best-effort; for strict consistency we recommend cache invalidation hooks via control-plane event API (we can add a lightweight invalidation call placed on the control-plane to notify affected sites).

Irene/Soojin/Jonas — can you call out any non-obvious constraints (network ports, expected SYN rates for scale, MTLS cert rotation cadence) before Tue? I attached an initial interface matrix and an ACL template we usually hand off to customers.

Proposed agenda for the review call (20-30m):
1) Review topology and traffic flows (5m)
2) Control-plane placement options + trust model (5m)
3) Data-plane egress and ACLs (5m)
4) Operational handoff (runbooks, cert rotation, monitoring) + action items (10m)

If Tue 19th at 10:00 PT is okay I’ll accept the invite.

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer

Thanks for pulling this together. I added inline notes to the diagram and exported a CSV of suggested egress ACLs for the three cluster tiers (on-prem-rack, colocation-edge, cloud-edge). Summary of technical concerns:

1) Ports and probes
- Control-plane API: TCP 8443 (HTTPS) + mutual TLS. We require a stable FQDN per control-plane and the cert must include SANs for the FQDNs used by data-plane nodes.
- KV cache sync: typically over gRPC on 7070; we can multiplex over the control-plane channel but recommend a separate port for observability.
- Health probes: allow ICMP/HTTP from the monitoring subnet to the data-plane nodes.

2) Egress minimization
- For explicit no-internet policies, the telemetry relay must be deployed inside the customer VPC (or a partner-provided collector inside the VPC). We can support compressed batch pushes every 30s to reduce sessions.

3) MTLS trust domains and cert rotation
- We recommend a short-lived cert rotation cadence for on-prem agents (7-14 days) with an automated bootstrap flow (the agent requests a bootstrap token from the control-plane which is signed once).
- For cross-site mTLS, use a control-plane-signed CA per customer; we do not recommend sharing CA across customers.

4) Consistency and cache invalidation
- If Acme needs strict global consistency for prompt caches, we will expose a synchronous invalidation API. That adds ~5-15ms tail latency for invalidation responses under normal load; test results included in the CSV notes.

Attachments included: egress-acls_v2.csv, network-interface-matrix.xlsx.

Action items before call:
- Acme: share the VPC CIDR ranges and proposed monitoring subnets.
- NetCloud: confirm whether the partner collector will be inside the Acme VPC or run as a tenant in NetCloud’s peered account.
- Redwood (Sóojin): prepare a TL;DR on cert rotation + bootstrap flow.

I’ll be on the Tue slot.

Regards,
